seoTitle: Connect a Namecheap Domain to Your Wix Website
metaDescription: Connect a Namecheap domain to Wix with the nameserver method: the Premium plan Wix requires first, the exact click path in both dashboards, and propagation timing.
intro: Buying a domain on Namecheap and building a site on Wix means those two platforms have to be told to talk to each other, and the usual way to do that is by pointing Namecheap's nameservers at Wix's. There is one requirement worth checking before any of that: Wix only connects a custom domain on a paid plan. Once that's out of the way, Wix's own wizard hands you the exact values to swap, and Namecheap's domain panel is where you paste them in. This guide follows that flow end to end, from the plan check through propagation.
prerequisites: A Wix Premium plan. Namecheap's own instructions state plainly that the site must be upgraded before a domain can be connected; the free Wix plan stays on a wix.com subdomain.
Owner access to the domain in your Namecheap account
costNote: Wix requires a paid Premium plan to connect any outside domain, so budget for that if the site is still on the free tier. Namecheap doesn't charge anything extra to point a domain you already own at another host.

steps.heading: Confirm the Wix site is on a Premium plan
steps.body: Wix's domain-connection option only becomes usable once the site is upgraded from the free plan; Namecheap's own support article states this as the first requirement. Check the plan under Wix Settings before doing anything else, and upgrade there if it's still free. Everything from this point assumes that's already done.

steps.heading: Open your Wix site dashboard
steps.body: Log into Wix and open the dashboard for the site you want the domain attached to. The left sidebar is the control centre here: Video Library, Apps, Site & Mobile App, Marketing, Analytics, Settings, and further down, Developer Tools. It's the same dashboard you'll return to later to confirm the domain connected. If you're partway through Wix's setup checklist, as shown by a progress tracker at the top, you can still jump into domain settings without finishing every item on that list first.

image.caption: The Wix site dashboard, with the sidebar navigation you'll use throughout setup, including Settings where domain connection lives.

steps.heading: Start the domain connection wizard in Wix
steps.body: From Settings, find the domain connection option and choose to connect a domain you already own instead of buying a new one through Wix. Wix runs a short numbered wizard, four steps in this flow, with step 3 asking you to find your current nameservers on your registrar's site (confirmed with an "I found them" checkbox) before moving you into the actual swap in step 4.

steps.heading: Copy the nameservers your own wizard shows you
steps.body: Step 4, "Replace your nameservers," lays out precisely what to remove and add, with copy buttons next to each value so you don't risk a typo. Wix is explicit that these values are account-specific: the pair shown to you may not match what someone else sees, so always copy the ones on your own screen instead of a pair quoted in a guide. In this recording the instructions called for removing dns1.registrar-servers.com and dns2.registrar-servers.com, Namecheap's default nameservers, and replacing them with the two Wix nameservers shown. The wizard also says you should end up with exactly two nameserver records; if your domain has more than two listed, remove the extras so only Wix's pair remains.

image.caption: Wix's nameserver swap instructions, showing the exact Namecheap default nameservers to remove and the two Wix nameservers to add in their place.

steps.heading: Update the nameservers in Namecheap
steps.body: Log into Namecheap, open Domain List from the left sidebar, and click Manage next to the domain you're connecting. Under the Domain tab, find the Nameservers section and use the dropdown to switch it from the default option to Custom DNS. Enter the two Wix nameservers from the wizard exactly as copied, one per line, then confirm with the green checkmark. No trailing spaces, no extra entries.

image.caption: Namecheap's Domain List, showing an active domain with its expiration date and the Manage button that opens its nameserver settings.

steps.heading: Confirm back in Wix and wait for propagation
steps.body: Return to the Wix wizard and click "I've replaced my nameservers" so Wix starts checking in the background; it can't verify the change instantly since it has to propagate first. Namecheap states changes typically take 24 to 48 hours to fully take effect, matching what Wix tells you to expect. Check the domain's status in Wix Settings periodically; it isn't broken just because it isn't instant. If it's still unconnected after two days, compare the nameservers in Namecheap against Wix's values character for character; a stray space or a leftover default entry is the usual cause.

troubleshooting.problem: The domain connection option isn't available in Wix
troubleshooting.cause: The site is still on Wix's free plan, and connecting an external domain requires a paid Premium plan.
troubleshooting.fix: Upgrade the site's plan from Wix Settings, then start the wizard again.

troubleshooting.problem: Namecheap shows the new nameservers saved, but Wix still says not connected after two days
troubleshooting.cause: Propagation is still catching up in some regions, or one of the entered values doesn't exactly match what Wix issued.
troubleshooting.fix: Compare each nameserver in Namecheap's Custom DNS fields against Wix's Settings page character for character, and wait out the full propagation window before assuming it's broken.

troubleshooting.problem: Email stopped working after the nameserver switch
troubleshooting.cause: Custom nameservers hand over all DNS control, including MX records that used to route mail through a different provider.
troubleshooting.fix: Recreate the mail records inside Wix's own DNS settings, or use Namecheap's DNS-records method instead of the nameserver method if you want to keep DNS at Namecheap.

faq.question: Does Wix require a paid plan to connect a domain?
faq.answer: Yes. Namecheap's own instructions state that the Wix site must be on a Premium plan before a domain can be connected; the free plan keeps the site on a wix.com subdomain.

faq.question: Should I use the nameserver method or a manual DNS method?
faq.answer: The nameserver method here is simpler, since Wix manages everything once the two nameservers are set. Namecheap also offers a DNS-records method for domains left on its BasicDNS or PremiumDNS, for people who want to keep other records under their own control.

faq.question: Will switching nameservers affect my email?
faq.answer: It can. Handing DNS control to Wix means any email-related records, MX records especially, that you had at Namecheap stop applying, so you'd need to recreate them through Wix's DNS settings.

faq.question: How long does propagation typically take?
faq.answer: Namecheap states 24 to 48 hours for a nameserver change to fully take effect, which matches what Wix's wizard tells you to expect.

faq.question: What exact values do I remove and add in Namecheap?
faq.answer: That depends on your own Wix account. Wix assigns nameserver pairs per account, so always copy the values shown on your own wizard screen instead of a pair you've seen in another guide.

faq.question: Can I switch connection methods later?
faq.answer: Yes, you can move from the nameserver method to a manual DNS-records setup or back again, though switching unnecessarily just adds more propagation waiting time.

verifiedNote: Click path and screens come from a recorded walkthrough. The nameserver values, the Custom DNS steps in Namecheap, and the propagation window were re-checked against Namecheap's and Wix's official support pages in September 2026. That check surfaced the Premium-plan requirement this guide previously left out entirely, and confirmed that Wix's nameserver pairs are assigned per account, not fixed, which the earlier version presented as a single universal pair.
